text: OFFICE OF THE VICE PRESIDENT
WASHINGTON
January 31, 1990
SWEARING-IN CEREMONY FOR THE
PRESIDENT'S COUNCIL OF ADVISORS FOR SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
February 2, 1990
(20 minutes)
Vice President’s EOB Office
FROM: Carnes Lord (A—
I. PURPOSE
To swear-in the 13 members of the President’s Council of
Advisors for Science and Technology.
II. BACKGROUND
By Executive Order, the President’s Council of Advisors for
Science and Technology (PCAST) was established on January 19,
1990. The Director of the Office of Science and Technology
Policy (OSTP) serves as Chairman of the Council which reports
directly to the President. The function of the Council is to
advise the President on matters involving all areas of science
and technology and to conduct a continuing review and assessment
of developments in science and technology. The PCAST replaces
the White House Science Council which reported to the Director -:
OSTP.
III. PARTICIPANTS
The Vice President
Selected OVP Staff
OSTP Staff
PCAST Appointees
IV. PRESS PLAN
Staff photographer; other to be determined by Dave Beckwith.

SUGGESTED TALKING POINTS--DR. BROMLEY'S SWEARING-IN
CEREMONY
Pre-Swearing-In
--The President and his entire administration are
firmly convinced that a healthy science,
engineering and technology enterprise is a key
ingredient for the future health and strength of
the nation. Evidence of that commitment is
abundant:
--The President has upgraded the position of
Science Advisor to that of Assistant to the
President for Science and Technology, and has
named your distinguished Chairman, Dr. Allan
Bromley, to the post. It has been a long time
since science input has been valued so highly
by the Chief Executive.
--The President has asked me, as Vice
President, to chair the Space Council and the
Competitiveness Council, again reflecting his
conviction that science and technology must be
integral components of policy.
--The President has created PCAST--you folks--
to advise him directly on all matters
involving science and technology. Very few
advisory groups report directly to the
President. I believe you are the first
science group to do so since more than 15
years ago.
Post Swearing-In
--Now that you're on board, let's get to work!
--Our '91 budget is a good one for science and
technology. We've worked hard to put it
together and we're proud of it. I know that
we can count on you, as representatives of
your respective communities, to help assure
that the Congress responds effectively.
--When we meet tomorrow at Camp David, we will
be discussing several issues of critical
importance to the nation. Three of these I
would mention in particular:
o  math and science education;
o  science and technology and economic
growth; and
o  the environment and global change.
--With the President and his outstanding
Science Advisor, I look forward to our
discussions.
Chairman Bromley, Vice Chairman Healy, members of
the Council, I wish you well.
